facts.statement: Quetecsaurus means "fire lizard" and is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Quetecsaurus (meaning "fire lizard", from the Milcayac word "quetec") is a genus of titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur

facts.statement: Quetecsaurus fossils are known from the Late Cretaceous of the southern Mendoza Province in western Argentina.
facts.quote: known from the Late Cretaceous of the southern Mendoza Province, western Argentina

facts.statement: Quetecsaurus was first described and named by Bernardo González Riga and Leonardo Ortiz David in 2014.
facts.quote: Quetecsaurus was first described and named by Bernardo González Riga and Leonardo Ortiz David in 2014

facts.statement: The humerus of Quetecsaurus has a unique shape featuring a strongly S-shaped proximal border, a rounded proximomedial border, and an angular proximolateral corner.
facts.quote: Its humerus is uniquely shaped, with strongly sigmoid (S-shaped) proximal border, rounded proximomedial border, and angular proximolateral corner

facts.statement: Quetecsaurus is classified within Titanosauria and is considered most closely related to Mendozasaurus and Futalognkosaurus, which are members of Lognkosauria.
facts.quote: Quetecsaurus was assigned to the Titanosauria, and considered to be most closely related to Mendozasaurus and Futalognkosaurus, members of Lognkosauria

facts.statement: Preliminary phylogenetic analysis places Quetecsaurus as a sister taxon to the clade formed by Mendozasaurus and Futalognkosaurus.
facts.quote: A preliminary phylogenetic analysis supported this assignment, placing Quetecsaurus as a sister taxon of the clade formed by Mendozasaurus and Futalognkosaurus

facts.statement: Quetecsaurus lived during the Turonian stage of the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 93 to 89 million years ago.
facts.quote: vivió a mediados del período el Cretácico durante el Turoniense, hace aproximadamente entre 93 a 89 millones de años

facts.statement: The holotype was collected from mudstones of the Cerro Lisandro Formation in the Neuquén Basin, dating to the middle or late Turonian stage of the Upper Cretaceous.
facts.quote: El holotipo fue recolectado de lutitas de la formación Cerro Lisandro, en la cuenca de Neuquén, que data de mediados o finales de la etapa del Turoniense del Cretácico Superior

facts.statement: This specimen represents the first sauropod with well-preserved materials recovered from the Cerro Lisandro Formation.
facts.quote: El espécimen representa el primer saurópodo con materiales bien preservados recuperado de esta formación

facts.statement: Quetecsaurus is related to Mendozasaurus and Futalognkosaurus based on the presence of three lateral laminae on its neural spines.
facts.quote: basándose en la presencia de tres láminas laterales en sus espinas neurales

facts.statement: The time range for Quetecsaurus is the Turonian stage, from 93.9 to 89.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Turonian (93.9 to 89.8 million years ago)
